title: Lesson 9 - Creating, Activating, and Executing Prompt Templates
description: Explain the process for creating, activating, and executing prompt templates.

questions.question: Which two associations does a Field Generation prompt template require when you create it?
options: An object and the specific field to complete
A flow and an Apex class
A data space and a search index
A channel and an agent user
questions.explanation: A Field Generation template helps a user complete a specific field, so it requires both the associated object and the field to complete, while the other template types need only the object.

questions.question: How do you invoke an activated prompt template from a Flow?
options: By pasting the prompt text into a formula resource
By calling it from an Apex trigger only
By adding an Actions element and picking the template from the Prompt Template category
By exporting the template and uploading it to the flow
questions.explanation: Every saved and activated template is exposed as an invocable action, so you add an Actions element and filter by the Prompt Template category, passing the associated record as a related entity where the template needs one.

questions.question: What does the resolved prompt show when you click Save and Preview?
options: The compiled agent graph the runtime executes
The template with its merge fields replaced by the selected record's real data, which is what is sent to the LLM
The list of versions saved for the template
The permission sets that can see the template
questions.explanation: The resolved prompt is the template after prompt resolution replaces the placeholders with real org data, and it represents exactly what reaches the LLM, which is why testing it against a sample record matters.
